Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mediaplanr 0.3.0

The agent can be scored and checked: its proposals map onto the response models that score them, and are checked against one shared definition of “allowed”.

New features

  • model_map() assigns every line item exactly one response model from a list fitted at mixed grains: of the models whose named values match, the most specific wins. A tie is an error naming both models; a line item no model covers is warned about, with the unmodeled share. Blank cells in the model list mean “any value”.
  • spend_by_model() sums each model’s spend by day, week or month – the input a response-model forecast needs. Unmodeled spend is kept under model_id = NA, so totals always reconcile. Data frames in and out; no dependency on mrmopt.
  • PlanConstraints, built with plan_constraints() from the rule_*() constructors or a rules sheet, holds the group rules a plan lives under: minimum and maximum spend or share, a fixed total with free phasing, and maximum change (an amount or a fraction) from a reference plan.
  • check_constraints() measures a plan against those rules, day by day, reporting each rule’s actual, limit, slack and whether it holds. A violation is warned about, never refused. constraints_schema() gives the rules as a JSON Schema, and plan_to_json() / plan_from_json() round-trip a PlanConstraints.
  • describe_plan() gains models (coverage, and the largest unmodeled line items) and constraints / reference (rules broken, and rules holding with no slack left).
  • The agency example ships with its response models and rules: agency_models.csv and agency_constraints.csv in extdata.
  • New vignette("agentic_planning"): one turn of an agent’s loop on the agency plan – describe, propose, a refusal and a retry, score, check, and hand to a person to approve.

mediaplanr 0.2.0

The agent can act safely: a plan can be inspected compactly, edited only through validated operations, held to its commitments, checked against its budget, and audited afterwards.

Breaking changes

  • @revision is gone. A plan’s revision is now derived from its lineage – its place among the approved plans on its branch – by lineage(). revise(revision = ) errors pointing there, and media_plan_from_df() no longer takes revision. Record an approval with revise(status = "approved", approved_on = ) instead.
  • JSON is now schema version 4. Files from versions 1-3 still read; a stored revision is ignored.
  • Every op is checked before any is applied, so in a list of ops a malformed later op is reported before a plan-dependent problem in an earlier one.
  • Op checking is stricter, and the same however the op was written:
    • add refuses during, which it used to ignore.
    • set, scale and total refuse negative values up front.
    • A during or restage window refuses fields other than from and to.
    • add needs both flight_start and flight_end, or neither.
  • A flight_id named on a single-period add no longer attaches the new row to an existing flight.
  • A ScenarioSet and attach_subplan() refuse plans whose @spend_basis differs.

New features

  • Op constructors and schema. op_set(), op_scale(), op_delta(), op_delta_each(), op_total(), op_transfer(), op_add(), op_drop(), op_shift(), op_restage() and op_rebound() build the same plain list a hand-written op is, and check it where it is written. plan_ops_schema() gives the same rules as a JSON Schema; with a plan, it narrows targets to the plan’s values, the contract to hand an agent.
  • transfer moves an amount between two sets of rows, leaving the plan’s total unchanged, as one op. A destination that plans nothing is filled evenly by in-market days.
  • Spend bounds. Optional min_spend / max_spend columns (bound_cols()) record commitments, floors and caps. Every edit respects them: group edits route around a bound, per-row edits are refused at one, and drop, shift and restage respect them too. They change only through the new rebound op. line_item_summary() reports committed_spend and headroom.
  • Provenance. A derived plan records the edits that produced it in @edits – replaying them on the parent reproduces it exactly – and why, in @rationale (author, goal, constraints id, forecast, notes), set with build_scenario(rationale = ). edit_log() reads a set’s records as a change log.
  • describe_plan(): a compact summary of a plan for an agent’s context – identity, shape, spend by column, commitments, units, spend by month, and what an op may target – capped so it stays a few kilobytes at any size.
  • Approvals. @approved_on records when a plan was approved. lineage() gains approved_on, revision and current; current_approved() returns the plan the set is buying against; and compare_scenarios() takes against = "base" | "parent" | "current_approved".
  • @spend_basis declares what the figures measure ("media_net", "client_net", "gross", …). A declaration, never a conversion.
  • check_budget() checks a plan against a budget envelope – windows and amounts naming any subset of the line item columns – day by day, warning on any row off by more than a tolerance. describe_plan(budget = ) summarises it.
  • The example agency plan used throughout the tests ships as system.file("extdata", "agency_plan.csv", package = "mediaplanr"), and vignette("getting_started") walks through it end to end.

mediaplanr 0.1.0

  • First version: typed media plans at a configurable grain, flights, units, scenarios and comparison, subplans, and JSON serialization.
